sentence: This project studies how a signaling pathway in excitatory neurons of mice affects brain inflammation and excitability after brain injury.
This project gets a cell sorter to help analyze rare cell populations in cancer, infectious diseases, and brain health.
This project builds an imaging system that uses light and no dyes to check blood flow and whether skin flaps after mastectomy stay alive.
This project measures tumor DNA circulating in plasma of patients with arthritis caused by immune checkpoint inhibitors to see whether it tracks cancer progression.
This project studies tau protein aggregates in the brain and how immunotherapy could target toxic tau oligomers.
This project gathers families affected by Alzheimer's disease, stores their biological samples, and shares clinical and genetic data with researchers.
This project studies DNA methylation in blood to see how it is linked to colorectal cancer and whether it could help prevent that cancer.
This project studies how changes in one gene affect gene regulation and brain development, using stem cell models and mice.
This project uses a microfluidic assay to study why platelets fail after traumatic injury and how platelet transfusion affects clotting in patient samples.
This project studies human liver transplant samples to learn how donor quality and preservation methods affect ischemia-reperfusion injury and outcomes after transplant.
This project studies how an enzyme that repairs DNA triggers an antiviral response in human cells and whether it can help cancer immunotherapy.
This project uses imaging to study how cerebrospinal fluid flows through the human brain and how that flow changes in aging and Alzheimer's disease.
This project studies smooth muscle problems in Duchenne muscular dystrophy and compares how different muscle types respond to treatment within the same animals.
This project studies how T cells in the gut and blood learn to fight Salmonella and Shigella after infection or vaccination in children and adults.
This project studies how healthy mitochondria in beta cells of the pancreas help make insulin and control blood sugar, and so prevent diabetes.
This project builds an imaging agent that shows levels of an immune checkpoint protein in the body to guide immunotherapy for lung cancer.
This project uses a large clinical-genomic database to study how patients given immunotherapy or with rare mutations respond to treatment.
This project studies how to connect nephrons to collecting ducts in kidney organoids made from stem cells so they work better.
This project studies how chemicals and tobacco products cause cancer and looks for biomarkers and food products that lower cancer risk.
This project studies how methamphetamine damages dopamine neuron circuits in the brain and how that may lead to addiction.
